messages.subject: INLA (Reached Numerical Limit!) BAPC example
parts:
Dear respected community members,
I am trying to utilize the INLA/BAPC combo to project age-standardized rates over a 10-year period for cancers.

When using the example presented by BAPC (show in the code below) it only works when the stdweights are removed.

"require(INLA)
  data(FemLCSweden)
  data(FemPYSweden)
  data(whostandard)
 
  lc_sweden <- APCList(FemLCSweden, FemPYSweden, gf=5)
 
  result  <- BAPC(lc_sweden, predict=list(npredict=10, retro=TRUE),
                  verbose=FALSE)
  
  result2  <- BAPC(lc_sweden, predict=list(npredict=10, retro=TRUE),
                  verbose=TRUE, stdweight=whostandard[6:17,2])

ERROR for result2:
"Iter=5 |grad|=0.0492 |x-x.old|=0.0104 |f-f.old|=0.00223(pass) Reached numerical limit!
Smart optimise part II: estimate gradient using central differences
Smart optimise part II: restart optimiser
maxld= -1764.832 fn= 92 theta= 4.382 10.248 9.604 6.256 [13.7, 0.03]"

After iteration 5, my INLA crashes and the sample model with standardized weights doesn't register. It should also be noted that INLA crashes, re-runs with improved values, and stops at this error.

This should be a "model" example, thus, I am not sure if the model parameters themselves (within BAPC) are the problem.

Is this a problem from within INLA or is it a lack of compatibility between INLA and BAPC

My BAPC, INLA, and R versions are all updated.

Thank you for your time and advice,

Sincerely yours,
